case_number: CIVIL APPEAL NOS.8598−8599 OF 2022 (Arising out of Special Leave Petition (C) Nos.11730−11731 of 2021)

parties.petitioner: T.J. Parameshwarappa @ Parameshwarappa @ J.T. Parameshwarappa @ Talalkena Gowdra Parameshwarappa
parties.respondent: The Branch Manager, New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Ors.

summary: The appeal challenged the Karnataka High Court's reduction of compensation from Rs.21,08,400 to Rs.7,37,604 in a motor accident claim. The appellant, injured in a 2015 accident while working as a cleaner, claimed permanent disability (54%) and loss of earnings, asserting inability to work. The High Court reduced disability to 20% and lowered notional income from Rs.18,000 to Rs.9,000/month. The Supreme Court considered correct assessment of permanent disability and future loss of earnings, referencing Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar for principles on just and adequate compensation to restore claimant's pre-accident position.
legal_provisions_cited: Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar and Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair [(1969) 3 SCC 64 : AIR 1970 SC 376]
R.D. Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. [(1995) 1 SCC 551 : 1995 SCC (Cri) 250]
final_judgment: Appeal allowed. Compensation award reinstated as per the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal's original assessment of Rs.21,08,400 with 8% interest, rejecting the High Court's reduction as incorrect in principle and quantum.
